description: A battalion S-4 logistics officer must issue the daily internal transport board, assigning four specialized vehicles to four routine support moves and recording the coordination actions required before dispatch.

shared_context.S1: Today's internal support board has four moves: clinic cold-storage cases to the medical annex, a communications mast to the north relay point, a generator to the engineering yard, and routine administrative pallets to the headquarters warehouse.
shared_context.S2: The available vehicles are one refrigerated van RV-2, one flatbed F-7, one 5-ton truck T-5, and one 2.5-ton truck T-2; each vehicle can support only one of the four moves today.
shared_context.S3: Maj. Okafor issues the binding vehicle assignments and dispatch board for these moves.
shared_context.S4: The unit's daily dispatch routine is to conduct a transport-board huddle before assignments are issued, with the transportation, medical, signal, and engineer representatives asked to report any load or vehicle-control requirements.

PF1.text: The transportation section's load sheet confirms that the communications mast is 24 feet long and must be carried on flatbed F-7 with its approved tie-down kit; SFC Miller received the corrected dimensions during yesterday's vehicle check, but the revised load sheet has not yet been posted to the dispatch board.

PF2.text: The clinic's cases contain temperature-sensitive specimens that must remain in the powered refrigerated compartment for the entire move, so the clinic load must use RV-2; Capt. Shah confirmed the handling instruction with the clinic this morning, but the medical movement note has not yet reached the S-4 folder.

PF3.text: The communications mast requires the signal section's certified tie-down inspection before release, and that inspection can be performed only on flatbed F-7; Lt. Brooks logged the certification requirement after checking the equipment record this morning, but it is not yet on the dispatch checklist.

PF4.text: The engineering generator weighs 5,200 pounds with its installed fuel tank and therefore requires 5-ton truck T-5; SFC Alvarez verified the weight from the current equipment book this morning, but the engineering load amendment has not been entered in the vehicle request.

acceptance_conditions: The clinic cold-storage cases must be assigned to RV-2.
The communications mast must be assigned to F-7.
The engineering generator must be assigned to T-5.
The administrative pallets must be assigned to T-2.
A refrigerated-compartment verification commitment for the clinic move must be recorded.
A certified tie-down inspection commitment for the communications mast must be recorded.
A vehicle-capacity confirmation commitment for the engineering generator must be recorded.
The corrected vehicle load sheet must be posted before dispatch.
The certified tie-down requirement must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'refrigerated_compartment_verification' and c['target'] == 'clinic_cold_storage' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'certified_tie_down_inspection' and c['target'] == 'communications_mast' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'vehicle_capacity_confirmation' and c['target'] == 'engineering_generator' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The corrected 24-foot dimension changes the communications-mast assignment to F-7 and requires the corrected load sheet to be posted.
The temperature-sensitive specimens change the clinic assignment to RV-2 and require refrigerated-compartment verification.
The vehicle-specific certification requirement changes the release procedure by requiring a certified tie-down inspection on F-7, and it is the fact that must be cited.
The exact 5,200-pound generator weight changes its assignment to T-5 and requires a vehicle-capacity confirmation.
